c.tagline: The 'Pearl of the South', Paraguay's river-beach and Carnival capital.

taxi.fareNote: Street taxis are largely unmetered, so agree the fare before setting off; the local MUV app (and limited Uber) give upfront prices, and city buses are the budget option.

emergency.note: 911 is Paraguay's unified emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the Carnaval crowds and along the busy costanera on summer nights.

hood_desc: The downtown core around the Cathedral and the main commercial streets, rebuilt into a modern grid of wide avenues after the Yacyretá dam flooded the old 'Zona Baja'; best for first-timers wanting shops, markets and services within walking distance.

The waterfront tourist zone on the Costanera with San José Beach, Paraguay's most popular river beach, backed by restaurants, bars and the Sambadrome that hosts the Encarnaceno Carnival; the liveliest and most convenient base for visitors.
A calm residential neighbourhood of leafy streets and family homes set back from the river; suits travellers wanting a quiet, local base near the centre.
A largely residential and commercial district near the bus terminal and main access roads; a practical, quiet base for onward travel to Asunción or the Jesuit ruins.
A newer beach and residential area to the west along the Costanera with Chaipé Beach and open riverside space; suits travellers wanting quieter sands away from the main crowds.
lodging: De la Trinidad Hotel Casino Resort

water.note: City tap water is treated, but most visitors stick to bottled.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 05:00 to around 22:30; taxis and ride apps fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Encarnación has no metro or tram; the city runs on local buses, taxis and ride apps like MUV, with a very walkable Costanera waterfront and downtown.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash (guaraníes) to the driver; there is no smartcard system.

air: Teniente Amín Ayub González Airport (ENO) — limited regional flights
Libertador General José de San Martín Airport (PSS), Posadas, Argentina — nearest full-service airport
Silvio Pettirossi International Airport (ASU), Asunción — main international gateway
bus: International buses across the San Roque González bridge to Posadas, Argentina
Long-distance coaches to Asunción and Ciudad del Este
train: Posadas–Encarnación International Train (cross-border shuttle over the bridge)

tip.r: Tipping is not obligatory; rounding up or leaving around 10% at restaurants for good service is appreciated but not expected.
